steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Durkheim (1858-1917): founding figure of sociology. Key ideas: social facts (external forces that constrain behaviour - laws, norms, religion), collective conscience (shared beliefs and values binding society together), anomie (normlessness when social regulation breaks down). Studied suicide rates to show social factors influence even the most personal act.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marx (1818-1883): society is shaped by class conflict. Key ideas: historical materialism (economy shapes society), alienation (workers are disconnected from their labour under capitalism - they don't own what they produce), false consciousness (workers don't realise they are exploited), revolution (the proletariat will overthrow capitalism creating a classless society).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Weber (1864-1920): society cannot be reduced to economics alone. Key ideas: rationalisation (modern society is dominated by efficiency, calculation and bureaucracy - an 'iron cage'), the Protestant Ethic (Calvinist beliefs about predestination encouraged hard work and saving, creating capitalism), verstehen (understanding social action by interpreting the meanings people attach to it).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Comparing the classical thinkers: Durkheim focused on social facts and consensus; Marx focused on class conflict and exploitation; Weber focused on meaning and rationalisation. Durkheim and Marx are structural (society shapes individuals); Weber combines structural analysis with understanding individual meanings.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe Durkheim's key ideas and evaluate their relevance to modern society. | Compare Marx and Weber on the causes of capitalism. | Evaluate which classical sociologist provides the most useful explanation of modern society.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Durkheim = SOCIAL FACTS + ANOMIE (consensus breaks down). Marx = CLASS CONFLICT + ALIENATION (exploitation). Weber = RATIONALISATION + PROTESTANT ETHIC (meaning + bureaucracy). Durkheim and Marx = structural (society shapes you). Weber = both structural and interpretivist (meaning matters too). Each classical thinker explains a DIFFERENT aspect of society. Combine them for a full picture.
